044
045import java.lang.System.Logger;
046import java.text.ParseException;
047import java.util.ArrayList;
048import java.util.List;
049import java.util.Objects;
050import java.util.function.BiFunction;
051import java.util.stream.Collectors;
052
053import javax.swing.JFormattedTextField;
054import javax.swing.JFormattedTextField.AbstractFormatter;
055import javax.swing.text.MaskFormatter;
056
057import dev.visdb.seesaw.datasources.RSC;
058import dev.visdb.seesaw.utils.JStuff;
059
060import static dev.visdb.seesaw.utils.JStuff.sf;
061import static java.lang.System.Logger.Level.*;

063/**
064 * A FormatterFactory, with formatters based on MaskFormatter, which uses
065 * getAllowNull() from the SSFormattedTextField to determine when
066 * a NullFormatter should be provided. In addition, the
067 * formatted text field is monitored and its value is changed
068 * to null/String as needed. This factory only specifies the default formatter,
069 * so edit and display formatters use the default formatter.
070 * <p>
071 * These formatters internally use a String value and the supplied converter
072 * is used to do the final conversion to a value of the correct type.
073 * Typically an AbstractFormatter is
074 * provided to convert objects to/from strings; see the code snippet below.
075 * The converter may not be needed if the value objects are a string.
076 * <p>
077 * Here's a code snippet that creates a {@link MaskFormatterFactory}
078 * that handles a {@link java.util.Date} field.
079 * {@snippet :
080 *     new MaskFormatterFactory.Builder<>("##/##/####")
081 *             .converter(new DateFormatter(new SimpleDateFormat("MMddyyyy")))
082 *             .placeholder('_').build();
083 * }
084 * With this snippet, if the text field has AllowNull true and the Value is
085 * null, then the text field is empty/blank; if the user then enters "1",
086 * the text field displays "1_/__/____"/; if then backspace, the field
087 * becomes blank.
088 * The placeholder and maskLiterals are used
089 * when determining if the text field's value should be null;
090 * in particular, when it would contain "__/__/____" the value is set to null
091 * and the text field is empty; though conceivable, it is not simple to
092 * automatically determine the literals.
093 * Also note that the converter's format does not
094 * contain "/" because in this example the factory's
095 * {@link MaskFormatter}'s ValueContainsLiteralCharacters is false.
096 * <p>
097 * Finer control over the edit input characters can be obtained by
098 * overriding the Builder's getSSMaskFormatter to create a
099 * subclass of SSMaskFormatter which has a custom DocumentFilter. For example:
100 * {@snippet class=SSMaskFormatterFactorySnippets region=init1}
101 * <p>
102 */
103@SuppressWarnings("serial")
104public class MaskFormatterFactory extends FormatterFactory {
105  /** Logger for component */
106  private static final Logger logger = JStuff.getLogger();
107
108  /**
109   * To build a new FormatterFactory with the specified parameters. Unless noted,
110   * a parameter is used when constructing the MaskFormatter.
111   *
112   * @param <T>
113   * @see <em>Effective Java</em> Item 2 about override.
114   * @see <a href="https://www.baeldung.com/java-builder-pattern-inheritance">
115   * Baeldung's java-builder-pattern-inheritance</a>
116   */
117  public static class Builder<T extends Builder<T>> extends FormatterFactory.Builder<T> {
118    // Required params
119    private final String mask;
120    // Optional params
121    private String validCharacters = null;
122    private String invalidCharacters = null;
123    private String placeholder = null;
124    private Character placeholderCharacter = null;
125    private boolean valueContainsLiterals = false;
126    private BiFunction<List<String>, RSC, Boolean> stringValidator;
127
128    /**
129     * Create the builder.
130     * @param mask Formatter's mask
131     */
132    public Builder(String mask) {
133      this.mask = mask;
134    }
135
136    /**
137     * formatter
138     * @param val
139     * @return  builder
140     */
141    public T validCharacters(String val) {
142      validCharacters = val;
143      return self();
144    }
145    /**
146     * formatter
147     * @param val
148     * @return  builder
149     */
150    public T invalidCharacters(String val) {
151      invalidCharacters = val;
152      return self();
153    }
154    /**
155     * formatter
156     * @param val
157     * @return  builder
158     */
159    public T placeholder(String val) {
160      placeholder = val;
161      return self();
162    }
163    /**
164     * formatter
165     * @param val
166     * @return  builder
167     */
168    public T placeholderCharacter(char val) {
169      placeholderCharacter = val;
170      return self();
171    }
172    /**
173     * formatter
174     * @param val
175     * @return  builder
176     */
177    public T valueContainsLiterals(boolean val) {
178      valueContainsLiterals = val;
179      return self();
180    }
181    /**
182     * Function that validates a string for the SSComponent, function returns
183     * false if not valid.
184     * After stringToValue, before converter.
185     * @param val function used to validate
186     * @return builder
187     */
188    public T stringValidator(BiFunction<List<String>, RSC, Boolean> val) {
189      stringValidator = val;
190      return self();
191    }
192
193    /**
194     * create the factory
195     * @return the factory
196     */
197    public MaskFormatterFactory build() {
198      return new MaskFormatterFactory(this);
199    }
200
201    /**
202     * Override this to provide custom SSMaskFormatter.
203     * @return
204     * @throws ParseException
205     */
206    // TODO: use builder not getConver...
207    protected SSMaskFormatter getSSMaskFormatter() throws ParseException {
208      Objects.requireNonNull(mask, "must specify mask");
209      SSMaskFormatter mf = new SSMaskFormatter(this);
210      if (validCharacters != null) {
211        mf.setValidCharacters(validCharacters);
212      }
213      if (invalidCharacters != null) {
214        mf.setValidCharacters(invalidCharacters);
215      }
216      if (placeholder != null) {
217        mf.setPlaceholder(placeholder);
218      }
219      if (placeholderCharacter != null) {
220        mf.setPlaceholderCharacter(placeholderCharacter);
221      }
222      mf.setValueContainsLiteralCharacters(valueContainsLiterals);
223
224      // NOTE:  following required to flip as needed
225      // DO NOT CHANGE
226      mf.setCommitsOnValidEdit(true);
227
228      // DO NOT CHANGE --- TODO: NEEDED?
229      mf.setValueClass(String.class);
230      return mf;
231    }
232  }
233
234  /**
235   * Create the factory, populate it with mask formatter.
236   * @param builder
237   */
238  protected MaskFormatterFactory(Builder<?> builder) {
239    super(builder);
240    try {
241      SSMaskFormatter mf = builder.getSSMaskFormatter();
242      setDefaultFormatter(mf);
243    } catch (ParseException ex) {
244      logger.log(ERROR, () -> "Bad mask format: " + builder.mask);
245    }
246  }
247
248  /**
249   * For a MaskFormatter simply slam the stringValue into the FormattedTextField.
250   * {@inheritDoc }
251   */
252  @Override
253  public void switchToNonNullValue(JFormattedTextField ftf, String stringValue)
254      throws ParseException {
255    ftf.setValue(stringValue);
256    if (logger.isLoggable(TRACE)) {
257      Object v = ftf.getValue();
258      logger.log(TRACE, () -> sf("switch: '%s' to %s %s", stringValue,
259                                 v != null ? v.getClass().getSimpleName() : null, v));
260    }
261  }
262
263  /** Uses setEditValid method to check that formatter should flip. */
264  @SuppressWarnings("serial")
265  public static class SSMaskFormatter extends MaskFormatter implements FormatterAssist {
266    /** MaskFormatter valid formatted input chars */
267    public static final String FORMATTING_CHARS = "#ULA?*H";
268
269    private final AbstractFormatter converter;
270    private final BiFunction<List<String>, RSC, Boolean> stringValidator;
271
272    /**
273     * Create the factory's MaskFormatter.
274     * @param builder (null is for testing)
275     * @throws ParseException
276     */
277    protected SSMaskFormatter(Builder<?> builder) throws ParseException {
278      super(builder != null ? builder.mask : "");
279      if (builder != null) {
280        this.converter = builder.getConverter();
281        this.stringValidator = builder.stringValidator;
282      } else {
283        this.converter = null;
284        this.stringValidator = null;
285      }
286    }
287
288    /**
289     *
290     * @return
291     */
292    @Override
293    public AbstractFormatter getConverter() {
294      return converter;
295    }
296
297    /**
298     *
299     * @return
300     */
301    public BiFunction<List<String>, RSC, Boolean> getStringValidator() {
302      return stringValidator;
303    }
304
305    /**
306     * The Format of the FormattedTextField.
307     * @return format
308     */
309    @Override
310    public SsFormat getSSFormat() {
311      if (getFormattedTextField() instanceof SsFormattedTextField ftf)
312        return ftf.getSsFormat();
313      return null;
314    }
315
316    /**
317     * If the value is not a String and there is a converter,
318     * then first convert the value before super.valueToString.
319     * @param value
320     * @return String representation of the value
321     * @throws ParseException
322     */
323    @Override
324    public String valueToString(Object value) throws ParseException {
325      String s = "";
326      if (value != null) {
327        if (value instanceof String string) {
328          // handle the case where where was null formatter
329          s = string;
330        } else {
331          if (getConverter() != null) {
332            s = getConverter().valueToString(value);
333          } else {
334            s = value.toString();
335          }
336        }
337      }
338
339      s = super.valueToString(s);
340      return s;
341    }
342
343    /**
344     * First convert the string with super.stringToValue,
345     * then use the converter (if there is one) to create
346     * the value object. This may be setEditValid arg.
347     * @param masked
348     * @return value for SSFTF
349     * @throws ParseException
350     */
351    @Override
352    public Object stringToValue(String masked) throws ParseException {
353      if (masked == null || masked.isBlank()) {
354        if (getFormattedTextField() instanceof SsFormattedTextField ftf && !ftf.getAllowNull())
355          throw new ParseException("Null value not allowed", 0);
356        return null;
357      }
358      // "string" is without mask caracters.
359      String string = (String) super.stringToValue(masked);
360
361      Object value = string;
362      if (getConverter() != null) {
363        value = getConverter().stringToValue(string);
364      }
365
366      if (getFormattedTextField() instanceof SsFormattedTextField ftf
367          && getStringValidator() != null
368          && !getStringValidator().apply(List.of(masked, string), ftf))
369        throw new ParseException("stringValidator failed", 0);
370
371      return value;
372    }
373
374    /**
375     * This method is invoked by the formatter when it is almost done.
376     * After super.setEditValid, if the text field does not have
377     * user input, set the value to null (which switches the formatter).
378     * @param valid
379     */
380    @Override
381    protected void setEditValid(boolean valid) {
382      super.setEditValid(valid);
383      // TODO: should this be done if not valid?
384      assistSetEditValidMaySwitchNull(getFormattedTextField());
385    }
386
387    // getMaskLiterals() is somewhat expensive. (not too bad, but my obsession)
388    // Cache the results. Monitor setMask and setPlaceholderCharacter
389    // to flush the parts of the cache as needed.
390
391    private LiteralsAndPositions maskLiteralsAndPositions;
392    private String maskLiterals_noPlaceholder;
393    private String maskLiterals_withPlaceholder;
394
395    /**
396     * {@inheritDoc }
397     */
398    @Override
399    public void setMask(String mask) throws ParseException {
400      super.setMask(mask);
401      maskLiteralsAndPositions = null;
402      maskLiterals_noPlaceholder = null;
403      maskLiterals_withPlaceholder = null;
404    }
405
406    /**
407     * {@inheritDoc }
408     */
409    @Override
410    public void setPlaceholderCharacter(char placeholder) {
411      super.setPlaceholderCharacter(placeholder);
412      maskLiterals_noPlaceholder = null;
413      maskLiterals_withPlaceholder = null;
414    }
415
416    private LiteralsAndPositions getMaskLiteralsAndPositions() {
417      if (maskLiteralsAndPositions == null)
418        maskLiteralsAndPositions
419            = FormatterAssist.getLiteralsAndPositions(getMask(), FORMATTING_CHARS);
420      return maskLiteralsAndPositions;
421    }
422
423    /**
424     * Find the characters in the specified {@linkplain MaskFormatter} that are
425     * displayed literally; there's a flag for including the placeholder character.
426     * These do not include the formatting characters like '#' or 'H';
427     * they are not displayed. Common examples are '/', '$'.
428     * Note that there is no consideration for chars beyond utf-16.
429     *
430     * @param includePlaceholder when true include the placeholderChar in result
431     * @return the literals in the mask
432     */
433    public String getMaskLiterals(boolean includePlaceholder) {
434      if (includePlaceholder) {
435        if (maskLiterals_withPlaceholder != null)
436          return maskLiterals_withPlaceholder;
437      } else {
438        if (maskLiterals_noPlaceholder != null)
439          return maskLiterals_noPlaceholder;
440      }
441      List<String> allLiterals = getMaskLiteralsAndPositions().literals();
442      if (includePlaceholder) {
443        allLiterals = new ArrayList<>(allLiterals);
444        allLiterals.add(String.valueOf(getPlaceholderCharacter()));
445      }
446
447      String noDuplicates = allLiterals.stream().distinct().collect(Collectors.joining());
448      if (includePlaceholder) {
449        maskLiterals_withPlaceholder = noDuplicates;
450      } else {
451        maskLiterals_noPlaceholder = noDuplicates;
452      }
453      return noDuplicates;
454    }
455
456    // For some reason, says it doesn't override anything when running javadoc.
457    // {@inheritDoc }
458    /**
459     * Most formats show extra characters that user use has not input.
460     * For a mask this probably includes mask literals and placeholder characters.
461     * @return characters not input by the user
462     */
463    @Override
464    public String getFormatLiterals() {
465      return getMaskLiterals(true);
466    }
467  }
468}
